messages:
marta: Heads-up — mkdocs linkcheck failed on main for /guides/deploy.md. Anchor '#scaling-scenarios' not found in rendered site.
samir: Can you paste the linkcheck output? I can take a look.
marta: Sure — here's the snippet:
```
Linkcheck: missing fragment: /guides/deploy.html#scaling-scenarios
File: docs/guides/deploy.md: heading 'Scaling scenarios' exists but slug resolves to 'scaling--scenarios'
```
jordan: Huh. We recently started embedding HTML comments above some headings for internal notes. MkDocs slugify seems to treat consecutive punctuation weirdly, turning space+hyphen into '--'.
emily: I ran `mkdocs build --strict` locally and hit the same. Quick fix: either remove the inline comment or add an explicit header id: `### Scaling scenarios {#scaling-scenarios}`. Prefer explicit id to be safe.
docs-bot: linkcheck report: 12 warnings, 1 error (deploy.md missing fragment). See CI run: https://ci.internal/1234
samir: If emily's ok to submit a PR I'll validate with the exact mkdocs version we use (1.5.3 + slugify plugin).
emily: I'll open a tiny PR that adds explicit ids to the affected headings and remove the problematic inline comment. Also adding a short note in docs/migration/anchor-behavior.md about slug behavior.
marta: Can you also add a line to the docs CI: linkcheck should fail on missing fragments (no exceptions) — otherwise these regressions sneak in.
jordan: Agreed. Also suggest a one-line test in the docs smoke job to run linkcheck on changed files only.
emily: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482 -- includes fix + migration note + CI tweak. Please review @samir @marta
samir: Reviewing now.
marta: Thanks — will merge after CI green. :thumbsup:
